title: Zephyrine and the Spire
premise: Wendell Delacroix, a memory-thief surviving in the magic-outlawed city of Vantrelle, has kept their head down for seven years by selling stolen memories as harmless charms. When the old gods resume answering prayers, Wendell's own stolen memories begin waking up—and one of them reveals a soul they sold years ago to the court beneath the mountain to buy their survival. To reclaim it before the last dragon-fire gutters out and the courts seal their bargains forever, Wendell must ally with a disgraced priestess and descend into a justice older than law. They win back the soul at the cost of every charm they ever stole, ending the book powerless but finally whole.
about_author: Yara Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a coastal city's municipal records. She writes fantasy about people who survive systems designed to erase them.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In Vantrelle's night market, Wendell sells a memory-charm to a grieving widow and feels something inside them stir—their oldest stolen memory is waking. A prayer whispered over their stall is answered by a god that hasn't spoken in decades. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine; invisibility beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Debt Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, with interludes from priestess Sable Ondine. The waking memory reveals seven-year-old Wendell sold their soul to the mountain court to escape a purge. Sable, exiled for heresy, recognizes the signs of returning gods and offers passage down. Emotional beat: shame confronting survival; the price of living surfaces.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, Guttering
chapters.summary: POV alternating Wendell and Sable as they descend through the court beneath the mountain, where souls are collateral and justice is bartered. The last dragon-fire dims as the courts move to finalize all outstanding bargains. Wendell must argue their own case before judges who remember them as property. Climax: Wendell stakes every stolen charm against the debt.

chapters.title: What the Fire Leaves
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The court accepts the bargain: every charm surrendered, every stolen memory returned to its owner, in exchange for the soul. Wendell climbs out of the mountain empty-handed but unowned, while the old gods' fire rekindles across Vantrelle. Resolution: powerlessness transformed into belonging; inheritance reclaimed rather than owed.
